n: At a January 1831 conference in Fayette, Saints questioned the command to move to Ohio. Christ answers as the Great I AM, who saw eternity and heaven’s angelic hosts before the world was made.

f.g: seraphs — a class of angels described by Isaiah.

n: He knows all things; past, present, and future are before his eyes. That is why his commands can be trusted.

f.w: all things are present before mine eyes

n: He spoke and the world was created; everything came through him.
Christ took Enoch’s city of Zion to himself, and he pleads for all believers before the Father by virtue of his shed blood.

f.w: have I pleaded before the Father for them

n: The rest of the wicked are held in “chains of darkness” until the final judgment.
Those who refuse his voice and harden their hearts face the same fate.
Christ watches over them and is among them, though they cannot see him.

f.w: I am in your midst and ye cannot see me

n: Soon the veil will be torn, they will see him, and the impure will not be able to endure that day.

f.w: the veil of darkness shall soon be rent

n: Prepare yourselves; the kingdom is yours, and the enemy will not win.
They are clean — though not all of them — and the Lord is pleased with them as a people.

f.w: ye are clean, but not all

n: All humankind is corrupted, and darkness prevails on earth before the hosts of heaven.
Heaven is pained and silent; angels await the command to harvest the earth and burn the tares. The enemy is united.

f.w: to gather the tares that they may be burned

n: The Lord reveals a secret: plots in “secret chambers” aimed to destroy them over time, which they didn’t know about.
They are blessed with this knowledge not because they are perfect — some are guilty — but because God is merciful to their weakness.
So be strong and fear not; the kingdom is theirs.
Hearing their prayers and the cries of the poor, God gives a commandment for their salvation. He made the rich and owns all; he favors no one.

f.w: I am no respecter of persons

n: God made the earth rich; it is his footstool, and he will stand on it again.
He offers greater riches: a land of promise “flowing with milk and honey,” free of any curse when he comes.

f.w: a land flowing with milk and honey

f.g: to graciously condescend to do something.

n: It will be their inheritance if they seek it with all their hearts.
God covenants that this land will be their inheritance and their children’s forever, and they will possess it again in eternity.

f.w: ye shall possess it again in eternity

n: Eventually they will have no human king; Christ will be their king.
Follow his voice, and they will be a free people under his law alone when he comes.
Teach one another according to your callings.
Let every person value others as themselves, practicing virtue and holiness.
The command is repeated for emphasis: esteem your brother as yourself.
A parable: what father of twelve obedient sons would dress one in robes and another in rags, and still call himself fair?
That is how God sees inequality among his children. “Be one; and if ye are not one ye are not mine” — a call to unity that underlies the law of consecration.

f.w: if ye are not one ye are not mine

n: Enemies in secret are seeking their lives.
They speculate about wars abroad but don’t understand the hearts of people at home. (The Civil War later came within their nation.)
Store up wisdom now, so they won’t learn these dangers the hard way. Those who are prepared need not fear — one of the most quoted lines on preparedness.

f.w: if ye are prepared ye shall not fear

n: Gathering will help them escape the enemy and become a pure, blameless people.
In Ohio, God will give his law (received weeks later as D&C 42) and endow them with power from on high — fulfilled partly in the Kirtland Temple.

f.w: there I will give unto you my law
endowed with power from on high

n: From there missionaries will go to all nations, for God has a great work: Israel will be saved and led wherever he wills.
Certain men will be appointed by the Church’s vote to handle matters in New York.

f.w: by the voice of the church

n: They will care for the poor and needy so they don’t suffer, and help them move to Ohio.

f.w: look to the poor and the needy

n: Their job is managing the Church’s property.
Farms that can’t be sold may be left or rented as owners think best.
Preserve everything; when elders are endowed and sent out, these resources will be gathered to the Church.
Seek the Father’s riches and be the richest people of all — rich in eternity. Earth’s riches are God’s to give. Beware of pride, as with the Nephites.

f.w: beware of pride, lest ye become as the Nephites of old

n: Every elder, priest, teacher, and member should work hard with their hands to accomplish God’s commands.

f.g: an old phrase meaning “get to work” or “set about it.”

n: Preaching should be a warning voice, neighbor to neighbor, in mildness and meekness.

f.w: the warning voice, every man to his neighbor

n: Leave the wicked behind; be clean, you who carry the Lord’s vessels — Isaiah’s call to Israel leaving Babylon.

f.w: Be ye clean that bear the vessels of the Lord
